title: Pelvic Floor and Kegels
summary: The pelvic floor is a sling of muscles that supports the bladder, bowel and (if present) the uterus. Kegel exercises strengthen it by repeatedly squeezing and releasing those muscles.
key_points: Can help with bladder control after childbirth or with age.
Some people find it improves sexual sensation and control.
steps: Find the muscles: they're the ones you would use to stop the flow of urine or hold in gas (don't routinely practise while urinating)
Squeeze for about 3–5 seconds, then relax fully for the same time
Repeat about 10 times, a few times a day, breathing normally
